question.problem: Two identical bins contain chips. The first bin contains four green and two yellow chips. The second bin has three green and one yellow chip. A bin is chosen at random, and a chip is selected from the chosen bin, also at random. If we know that the selected chip is green, what is the probability that it came from the second bin?
question.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be the event that the second bin is selected, and let $G$ be the event that a randomly selected chip is green. Then, we require $P(S|G),$ which we can compute using Bayes' theorem. 

$$
P(S|G)=\frac{P(G|S)P(S)}{P(G)}=\frac{P(G|S)P(S)}{P(G|S)P(S)+P(G|{S}^{′})P({S}^{′})}
$$

Note that ${S}^{′}$ is the event that the first bin is selected.

From the problem statement, we have the following:

- Since the first bin contains four green and two yellow chips, and the second bin contains three green and one yellow chip, we have

$$
P(G|S)=\frac{3}{4},\,P(G|{S}^{′})=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

- Since the bin is selected at random, we have

$$
P(S)=P({S}^{′})=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, using Bayes' theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(S|G) & =\frac{P(G|S)P(S)}{P(G|S)P(S)+P(G|{S}^{′})P({S}^{′})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2})}{(\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{4})}{(\frac{3}{4}+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{4})}{(\frac{17}{12})} \\  & =\frac{9}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$
